annotation.kind: source-faithful explicit-norm formulation of the LDL-transpose solution-phase backward-stability argument in Appendix B

assumptions: L is the nonsingular unit lower triangular factor used by the Appendix-B LDL-transpose solve, and D is its one-by-one/two-by-two block diagonal factor.
The premise p29LDLT L D = A + E0 and the bound on E0 are the factorization backward error established in the preceding part of Appendix B.
The block-D solve has the same normwise backward-stability hypothesis imposed by the paper; its perturbation level eta is shared identically by N and L.
The forward and transposed back solves are the explicit rounded recurrences under the standard relative-error model, excluding overflow and underflow, with n*u<1.
The entrywise-sum matrix norm and p29TotalBackwardBound expose one valid dimension-dependent coefficient hidden by the paper's d'(n)*epsilon and O(epsilon^2) notation.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P29 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P29 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p29_t2_ldlt_solve_backward_stability (fp : P29FPModel) (n : Nat) (A L D E0 : P29Matrix n n) (b z : Fin n -> Real) (eta factorEta : Real) ... : exists DeltaL DeltaD DeltaU F, componentwise triangular perturbation bounds and F = p29TotalBackwardError E0 L D DeltaL DeltaD DeltaU and (A+F)*xhat=b and p29EntryNorm F <= p29TotalBackwardBound fp n eta factorEta A L D
formal_statement.plain_language: A backward-stable factorization, rounded forward solve, backward-stable block-diagonal solve, and rounded transposed back solve compose into a single normwise perturbation F for which the computed vector exactly solves (A+F)x=b.

informal_proof: Obtain the componentwise backward perturbation for the forward solve, use the supplied block-D perturbation, and obtain the independent componentwise backward perturbation for the transposed back solve. Compose the three exact perturbed systems, add the factorization perturbation, expand the exact product, and bound all first- and higher-order terms by submultiplicativity of the explicit finite matrix norm.
informal_statement: The linear-solution backward-stability conclusion in Appendix B, retaining the preceding factorization perturbation and all three solution-phase perturbations with an explicit dimension-dependent bound.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 20(2), 1998, printed pages 513-561

absence_search.result: The compiled condition-L set has substantial forward- and back-substitution backward-error theorems but no Bunch--Kaufman, Bunch--Parlett, block-LDLT, or two-by-two block-solve theorem. Closer Chapter-11 block-LDLT declarations exist only in uncompiled frozen source and are unavailable to L. Mathlib has no floating-point triangular-solve theorem.
absence_search.scope: the complete frozen NumStability source, its compiled object list in metadata/library_olean.json, and Mathlib

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The generic mixed LU composition theorem consumes already-supplied triangular perturbations and does not produce the target's two rounded LDL-transpose solves or handle its intervening block-D solve. L therefore invokes the two separate substantial triangular-solve theorems. N reconstructs both recurrence analyses. Private proofs compile and are 374 lines in L versus 1444 lines in N.

tier_rationale: The proof directly needs two distinct substantial importable results: NumStability.forwardSub_backward_error and NumStability.backSub_backward_error. Neither is in Mathlib, and reconstructing both rounded triangular-solve analyses accounts for most of the 1444-line N proof. L reuses both and performs the paper-specific block-solve and factorization perturbation composition, producing a much larger speedup than T1.
